claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model should be certified for launch on the present record because aggregate launch readiness passed, the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the remaining segment-specific weakness can be handled through documentation and ongoing risk management.
decision_criteria: Use 'compliant' only if admissible evidence shows the materiality predicate is satisfied and the policy threshold for launch is met.
Use 'suspicious' when the packet has some support but a required support link remains unresolved; that applies here because materiality and required mitigation/approval are not closed.
Escalate to 'noncompliant' if evidence shows launch proceeded without required disclosure, without legal clearance where required, or without approved risk acceptance for a material weakness.
A compliant result would require evidence that the limitation was disclosed as required, resolved, or formally accepted before launch.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying release policy text or approval record showing whether disclosure alone is sufficient for launch in this case.
Provide any approved risk-acceptance decision covering the small-business onboarding gap before launch.
Provide the legal review outcome on whether disclosure is mandatory and whether launch may proceed before that review closes.
Provide evidence showing whether the two paid pilot commitments make this segment a named launch use case or contractual customer segment under policy.
specific_concerns: The policy text makes the weakness plausibly material because the affected small-business onboarding segment is named in two paid pilot commitments.
Legal review is still open on whether the gap must be disclosed, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
The Actor relies on aggregate readiness and rehearsal success, but those do not by themselves resolve materiality for a named customer segment.
No admissible evidence shows the limitation was resolved before launch or covered by approved risk acceptance, which the policy identifies as the relevant threshold.
Public model-card and risk-management guidance supports documentation practice, but it does not itself authorize certification under the stated release policy.
unsupported_claims: That the current record is sufficient to certify the model for launch.
That the remaining issue is only a documentation and monitoring matter rather than a potential launch-gating material limitation.
Any implication that aggregate pass status overrides the policy treatment of a weakness affecting named customer commitments.
